descriptionAr: Who are we? Cohere is the leading security-first enterprise AI company. We build cutting-edge foundation AI models and end-to-end products that are designed to solve real-world business problems. We’re training and deploying frontier models for enterprises who are building AI systems. We believe that our work is instrumental to the widespread adoption of AI and we are looking for folks that want to be part of that. We obsess over what we build. Each one of us is responsible for contributing to increasing the capabilities of our models and the value they drive for our customers. Cohere is a team of researchers, engineers, designers, and more, who are all passionate about their craft. We are a global technology company headquartered in Toronto with key offices in London, New York City, San Francisco, Montreal, Paris, Berlin and Seoul. Join us! Why this role? We're building the foundational infrastructure that will define how the world thinks about and deploys AI, and we want the sharpest, most driven, and most curious people to help us do it. As the founding lead of Agentic Analytics, a new team in our Analytics and Data Insights organization, you'll own how Cohere gets answers from its own data: an agentic analytics system that answers business questions over governed data, shows the source, query, and freshness behind every answer, and asks for clarification or declines when the evidence is insufficient. Agentic analytics is far from a solved problem, and correctness is the hard part. A query that runs can still answer the wrong question. Agents go wrong when a business term maps to more than one table, when data goes stale, and when the right context never reaches the model. The worst failures are silent and plausible: a join that double-counts, a wrong denominator, missing data read as zero. Getting this right takes governed definitions, context an agent can use, and an evaluation bar that decides what ships. You'll build on work already in motion: an internal analytics agent in pilot on our BigQuery warehouse, which is fed by tested ingestion pipelines and modeled in dbt. In your first year, you'll take it to production for teams across Cohere, one domain at a time, and make it replicable: each new domain stands up with configuration, a fresh evaluation set, and very little new code. This is a hands-on staff engineering role reporting to our Senior Director of Data Analytics. You'll write production code and evaluation sets yourself while managing a small founding team that grows as the system proves itself. You may have held the title software engineer, AI engineer, or data scientist; what matters is that you've built a system like this and run it in production. Responsibilities As the lead of Agentic Analytics, you will: Own the system end to end. Set the architecture for how a business question becomes a governed query and a verifiable answer: interpreting the question, retrieving the right context, applying approved definitions and joins, enforcing the asking user's permissions, and attaching the evidence (source, query, freshness) to every answer. Build and run it in production. Design the core services and write much of the first version yourself: agent-facing data tools (MCP or equivalent), context retrieval, agent skills for analytics, and the APIs that serve answers. Hold them to production standards for reliability, latency, cost, security, and observability. Put it where people already work: Slack, North, IDEs, and other agents. Hold every release to the evaluation bar. Build and run the evaluation harness, and define what correct means in each domain: ground-truth question sets, including held-out cases and questions the agent should clarify or decline; result-level scoring, correct-or-decline rates, coverage, and error severity; and regression tests on every change to context, skills, or models. Nothing ships below the bar, and the call on when a domain is ready for production is yours. Engineer the context layer. Turn metric definitions, approved joins, documentation generated from the code that builds each table, a business glossary, and worked examples into context the agent can use. Every correction becomes a reviewed definition and a regression test. Roll it out across Cohere. Bring domains such as marketing, revenue, finance, and product onto the system one at a time, each with named owners, certified definitions, and its own evaluation set. Measure adoption, accuracy, turnaround, and correction effort against how those teams work today. Make it replicable. Package the tools, skills, context templates, and evaluations, and document them well enough that other teams at Cohere can run the system without you. Hire and lead the team. Bring on the team's first engineers, set the technical bar, review the work, and develop the people doing it. Partner across Cohere. Work with our data platform team on the warehouse and semantic models, our model evaluation team on evaluation methodology, our security team on access, and each domain's owners on definitions and rollout. Qualifications You may be a good fit, if you have: 10+ years building and operating production analytics or software systems, including technical leadership of a team or of systems that span teams Experience shipping LLM agents to production: tool use, MCP or similar, retrieval and context engineering, guardrails, and observability, with firm opinions on where they fail Hands-on experience building natural-language or agentic analytics (text-to-SQL, analytics agents, question answering over a semantic layer) that real users relied on, and evidence that it was right Depth in evaluating LLM systems: golden sets, result-level comparison, abstention metrics, error taxonomies, and regression testing in CI, plus the judgment to tell a good demo from a system you'd put in front of a CFO Strong Python and SQL, and experience designing and running production services and APIs on a major cloud (Google Cloud is a plus)

descriptionAr: About Ramp Ramp is building the smart infrastructure for finance teams, embedded in the transaction flow of every dollar a business spends. We automate how over $275B in annualized spend flows in and out of 85,000+ companies: authorizing payments, flagging risk, categorizing spend, and closing books. The problems are high-stakes, data-dense, and unforgiving. We hire people with high agency and high urgency. We look for slope over intercept. We care less about where you trained and more about what you’ve built. At Ramp, everyone is a builder who owns problems end to end and makes consequential decisions that shape the outcome. The median Ramp customer saves 7.5% and grows revenue 16% in their first year – far in excess of businesses operating without Ramp. We believe every ambitious company deserves the same. If you want to build systems that directly shape how companies move and manage billions, Ramp is the place to do it. About the Role Every approval request, receipt reminder, payment alert, and card notification Ramp sends has to reach the right person, on the right channel, at the right time. When it does, finance teams close faster and employees spend less time chasing tasks. When it doesn't, a missed message can mean a stalled approval, a late payment, or a flood of notifications nobody asked for. Ramp's Communications Platform team builds the shared system that every product team uses to reach customers. It handles transactional messages across email, SMS, push, Slack, Microsoft Teams, and WhatsApp, including templating, delivery, retries, digesting, user preferences, and delivery monitoring. The team also supports the conversational experiences that let customers work with Ramp directly from the channels they already use. We're looking for a backend engineer to own a core part of that platform. You'll take responsibility for an area such as message delivery and channel integrations, communication preferences, or platform reliability and scale, set its technical direction within the team, and keep it correct and dependable as message volume and the number of teams building on it grow. You'll work closely with product, design, and engineering partners across Ramp to make communications faster, more reliable, and easier for every team to build on. What You'll Do Own the design and evolution of a core part of Ramp's communications platform, from technical design through launch, monitoring, and iteration Build and extend integrations with messaging channels and delivery providers, including email, SMS, push, and workplace chat tools such as Slack and Microsoft Teams Design delivery workflows that are idempotent, retry safely, and confirm successful delivery, so customers reliably get the messages they need without duplicate sends Build communication preferences and controls that let users and administrators decide what they receive and where Make the platform simple and safe for other Ramp engineers to build on, with clear abstractions, strong defaults, and good developer tooling Improve the reliability, performance, and observability of the platform as message volume grows Drive technical direction for your area and raise the engineering bar through design reviews, code reviews, and mentorship What You'll Need Experience designing, building, and operating production backend systems, including APIs, data models, and asynchronous workflows A track record of owning a system or product area end to end and shaping its technical direction over time Strong system design judgment, especially around reliability, idempotency, and correctness in high-volume distributed systems Product sense: you care about the experience of the people receiving each message, not just the ticket, and you balance speed with quality Clear communication and a collaborative approach to technical decisions across product, design, and engineering Nice to Haves Experience building notification, messaging, or communications platforms Experience integrating with messaging providers or channel APIs, such as Twilio, SendGrid, Slack, Microsoft Teams, or WhatsApp Experience building internal platforms or shared services used by many engineering teams Experience scaling high-volume, event-driven, or queue-based systems Benefits available to all full-time Ramp employees (Global) Flexible PTO Centralized home-office equipment ordering Health and wellness stipend Budget for intra-office travel Weekly coffee stipend United States 100% medical, dental & vision insurance coverage for you, with partial coverage for dependents One Medical annual membership 401(k), including employer match on contributions made while employed by Ramp Fertility HRA (up to $10,000 per year) Parental leave: up to 16 weeks (birthing + bonding) or 8 weeks (bonding only) at 100% pay Pet insurance In-office perks: lunch, descriptionAr: Replit is the agentic software creation platform that enables anyone to build applications using natural language. With millions of users worldwide, Replit is democratizing software development by removing traditional barriers to application creation. About the role: Make Replit the single place where businesses can buy everything they need through their agents. As a Staff Software Engineer on Replit’s Money team, you’ll set technical direction and build the commerce platform that lets users discover, evaluate, purchase, and manage the products and services they need to build and run their businesses—without leaving Replit. Replit already enables businesses to accept payments through integrations such as Stripe. This role builds on that foundation to expand what businesses can buy and accomplish through Replit Agent. You’ll design commerce experiences that combine the simplicity consumers expect with the controls enterprises need, making agent-assisted purchasing useful, trustworthy, and reliable. You’ll own architecture and lead cross-team delivery across merchant and service-provider integrations, agent tools, purchasing workflows, and the lifecycle after a transaction. The challenge goes beyond executing a payment: agents need to understand what a user wants, present clear choices and costs, act within delegated authority, and verify that the purchase delivered the intended outcome. You’ll stay hands-on with design and code while aligning partners, mentoring engineers, and turning an ambitious product vision into incremental customer value. You will: Set technical direction for Replit’s financial infrastructure, with an immediate focus on enterprise billing, spend controls, and financial correctness. Build shared services for usage-based billing, pricing, credits, subscriptions, and entitlements so product teams can launch without rebuilding billing. Automate enterprise contract lifecycles—from onboarding through amendments and renewals—keeping commercial terms, provisioned credits, and invoices in sync. Build timely budget enforcement, alerts, and overrides that give customers control over spend without disrupting their hosted apps. Make AI usage understandable: attribute costs to the right customer, workspace, user, or agent, including delegated work without double-counting. Build reconciliation and audit trails that make balances and invoices explainable and help Finance catch discrepancies before customers do. Simplify the billing stack through safe migrations that preserve balances, transaction history, and customer access. Own production reliability through testing, observability, incident response, and safe recovery from duplicate events, delayed usage, and partial failures. Stay hands-on while leading cross-team delivery, mentoring engineers, and partnering with Product, Finance, Sales, and Support. Required skills and experience: A track record of Staff-level technical ownership: setting architecture and delivering complex initiatives across teams. Deep experience building and operating production backend or distributed systems. Strong fundamentals in API design, data modeling, databases, and event-driven architecture. Sound judgment around transactions, consistency, concurrency, idempotency, and failure recovery. Experience evolving live systems and migrating data without compromising correctness or availability. Product judgment that balances customer needs, delivery speed, and long-term system quality. Clear communication with technical and non-technical partners, including translating business requirements into system behavior. Hands-on leadership through implementation, design reviews, mentoring, and production ownership. Preferred Qualifications Experience with billing, payments, subscriptions, credits, entitlements, or other financial systems. Experience with enterprise contracts, negotiated pricing, invoicing, or quote-to-cash automation. Experience with high-volume usage metering, pricing calculations, or low-latency spend controls. Experience building reconciliation, financial reporting, or auditable transaction histories with Finance and Accounting. Experience integrating billing, payment, or CRM platforms, with judgment about what to build versus buy. Bonus Points : Experience with AI or cloud infrastructure billing, including variable costs and attribution across distributed workloads. Experience building customer-facing spend visibility, budgets, or internal tools that reduce manual billing work. Experience with cloud marketplace billing, payment recovery, or fraud and dispute workflows. Familiarity with agentic commerce or delegated spending. These are additional strengths, not requirements. What we value : Customer outcomes: success means a business can get what it needs through its agent, with clear costs and a verified result—not merely a completed API call. User control and trust: agents act within explicit authority, surface consequential choices, and make purchases and ongoing commitments understandable. Consumer simplicity and enterprise readiness: straightforward experiences should coexist with the controls organizations need. End-to-end ownership: we own the experience from intent through purchase, fulfillment, and ongoing management. Pragmatic technical leadership: we build on what exists, deliver incremental value, and invest in correctness and extensibility where they matter. Clear collaboration: we document decisions, surface risks early, and help other teams and partners succeed. descriptionAr: About the Role As an Account Director for Higher Education in AMER, you will own strategic relationships with colleges, universities, and higher education systems as they move from AI experimentation to responsible, institution-wide transformation. Engage credibly with presidents, provosts, CIOs, CTOs, academic leaders, researchers, administrators, security teams, legal, procurement, finance, and end-user champions. Own new-business, subscription, and consumption revenue; forecast pipeline and usage-based growth; and use adoption, value realization, and expansion signals to manage the business. Develop durable executive relationships and a broad coalition of institutional champions across decentralized stakeholder groups. Represent OpenAI as a thoughtful partner at executive forums, industry events, customer advisory discussions, and the broader higher education ecosystem. Demonstrated ownership of consumption- or usage-based revenue, including forecasting usage, driving adoption, creating new use cases, and converting customer outcomes into expansion. The technical depth to learn complex AI products, lead effective discovery, partner closely with technical teams, explain technical concepts accurately at both executive and practitioner altitudes, and translate them into academic, operational, research, and commercial outcomes. Experience leading strategic transformations rather than isolated point-solution sales, including governance, change management, adoption, and measurable operational, academic, research, or user outcomes. Strong executive presence, structured communication, and the ability to earn trust across senior leaders, technical experts, faculty, administrators, and end users. Excellent account planning, qualification, negotiation, forecasting, and cross-functional orchestration skills. High judgment, curiosity, resilience, and comfort operating through ambiguity, product change, and evolving customer needs. A mission-driven approach to deploying AI responsibly and helping institutions build durable capability rather than short-lived pilots. descriptionAr: Who We Are Notion is the collaborative AI workspace where teams and agents think together . We're building one place where your knowledge, projects, meetings, and AI tools live side by side, so work is faster, clearer, and less fragmented. Millions of individuals, small teams, and large companies run their work on Notion. Notinos (our employees) are customer zero in bringing this future of work to life. We care about craft, building things that last, and the belief that great work is still fundamentally human. Our goal isn’t to ship the next feature. Each and every team of Notinos is working to set the standard for how humans work together in the AI era. From building a business’s system of record to making and managing AI agents to automating away the busy work, we care deeply about giving our customers more time for their life’s work. About the Role: Web Infrastructure builds the foundations behind Notion’s web clients so product engineers can ship fast, reliable, accessible experiences. As a junior engineer on the team, you’ll help make those experiences measurably faster and more resilient. You’ll investigate performance bottlenecks, improve how the client loads and responds, and help build tools that catch regressions earlier. You don’t need to arrive as a performance expert; we’re looking for strong fundamentals, curiosity, and a desire to learn by shipping useful work. This role can be based in either San Francisco or New York City. We work from our offices on Mondays, Tuesdays and Thursdays (our Anchor Days) because we do our best thinking and building together in person. We’re looking for someone who’s excited to work alongside the team during those days. What You'll Achieve: Use browser tools and real-world data to investigate page-load and interaction bottlenecks, then turn findings into focused improvements. Help build or improve performance tests, dashboards, and guardrails that make regressions easier to catch during development and rollout. Ship scoped improvements to client loading, rendering, asset delivery, or caching, measuring their impact and checking for regressions. Partner with Web Infrastructure and product engineers to land changes safely across Notion’s web clients. Document what you learn and share clear recommendations so teams can make better performance tradeoffs. Skills You'll Need to Bring: Solid programming fundamentals and some experience building software with JavaScript or TypeScript; familiarity with React or another component-based UI framework is helpful. Curiosity about how browsers work and how code affects page load, rendering, and interaction responsiveness. A thoughtful debugging approach: you can break a problem down, gather evidence, and ask for help when you’re stuck. Clear, kind communication and an interest in collaborating across teams. Intellectual curiosity about AI-enabled engineering tools; you use them thoughtfully and review their output critically. Experience with performance profiling, browser developer tools, React profiling, bundlers, code splitting, service workers, asset caching, or performance testing is a plus—not a prerequisite. We welcome candidates who are excited about the work even if they don’t match every bullet. Notion is committed to providing highly competitive cash compensation, equity, and benefits. The compensation offered for this role will be based on multiple factors such as location, the role’s scope and complexity, and the candidate’s experience and expertise, and may vary from the range provided below. For roles based in San Francisco or New York City, the estimated base salary range for this role is $150,000 - $168,000 per year. By clicking “Submit Application”, I understand and agree that Notion and its affiliates and subsidiaries will collect and process my information in accordance with Notion’s Global Recruiting Privacy Policy and NYLL 144 . #LI-Onsite A Note on AI You don’t need deep AI expertise for every role, but we do expect every Notino to be intellectually curious, drawn to tinkering and discovery, and excited to use AI as a real collaborator in their work. For some roles, AI fluency is a core requirement — when that’s the case, we'll say so explicitly in the qualifications. People who thrive here don’t treat AI as a novelty. descriptionAr: About the Team OpenAI’s Applied AI Engineering team helps organizations turn frontier AI capabilities into safe, reliable, and high-impact production systems. We work with customer executives, product and engineering teams, security leaders, and transformation teams to identify valuable opportunities, accelerate technical implementation, and scale what works. Production-ready deployments are defined by complexity rather than any one industry: existing architectures, diverse data environments, security and governance requirements, multiple stakeholder groups, and organization-wide change. We turn lessons from these deployments into better products and reusable patterns for customers everywhere. About the Role As an Applied AI Engineer you will partner directly with leading organizations to design, build, and deploy AI systems that deliver measurable business outcomes. You will combine deep technical judgment, hands-on engineering, and customer leadership to take ambitious ideas from use-case selection and architecture through prototyping, evaluation, production launch, and scale. You will write and debug code, build evaluation systems, resolve complex integrations, and guide decisions involving model behavior, reliability, latency, cost, safety, security, governance, and operational readiness. Success is measured by production systems, sustained adoption, and meaningful customer impact—not simply activity or successful demonstrations. This is a rare opportunity to work on consequential real-world deployments at the frontier of AI while directly influencing how OpenAI’s products evolve. This role is based in Munich/Berlin. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees In this role, you will: Partner directly with enterprise and digital native customers to identify high-value opportunities and translate them into technical architectures, implementation plans, evaluation strategies, and measurable success criteria. Design, build, and deploy AI systems that solve important customer problems and produce measurable business outcomes. Work hands-on in code to build prototypes, evaluation harnesses, reference implementations, integrations, and production accelerators. Make sound technical decisions across models, agents, retrieval, tools, data, reliability, observability, latency, cost, safety, security, and governance. Diagnose complex implementation challenges, reproduce failures, test hypotheses, and drive blockers toward resolution. Help customers progress from promising prototypes to reliable production systems, sustained adoption, and scaled impact. Partner closely with customer engineering teams and OpenAI Product, Research, Engineering, Security, and go-to-market teams, translating deployment experience into high-signal product feedback. Create reusable architectures, tooling, playbooks, and technical guidance that accelerate future enterprise deployments. You’ll thrive in this role if you: Have a demonstrated track record of 5+ years of designing, building, and delivering AI or machine-learning systems in enterprise environments, including taking systems from prototype to production. Relevant backgrounds may include applied AI or ML engineering, forward-deployed engineering, software engineering, customer engineering, solutions architecture, product engineering or technical consulting. Are fluent in both German and English Can point to substantial personal contributions in code, architecture, evaluation, debugging, or engineering of production systems—not only program or stakeholder management. Are highly proficient in Python and comfortable working across an AI application stack; experience with JavaScript, TypeScript, or another relevant language is valuable. Understand how to evaluate AI systems systematically using representative data, graders, production signals, and human judgment. Have navigated enterprise production requirements such as integrations, reliability, observability, security, privacy, data governance, performance, and cost. Can connect technical decisions to customer workflows, adoption, and measurable business outcomes. Communicate with clarity and credibility across hands-on engineers, technical leaders, security teams, product leaders, and executives. Bring high agency, strong technical judgment, and end-to-end ownership in ambiguous environments. Learn quickly, challenge assumptions constructively, and collaborate with humility; experience in a particular industry or with OpenAI products is not required. About OpenAI OpenAI is an AI research and deployment company dedicated to ensuring that general-purpose artificial intelligence benefits all of humanity. We push the boundaries of the capabilities of AI systems and seek to safely deploy them to the world through our products. AI is an extremely powerful tool that must be created with safety and human needs at its core, and to achieve our mission, we must encompass and value the many different perspectives, voices, and experiences that form the full spectrum of humanity. descriptionAr: About the team Most providers make customers migrate their data to them. We're doing the opposite: bringing ClickHouse Cloud into the environments our customers already trust, so their data stays useful right where it lives. Those environments come in a few shapes. Some are major cloud data platforms that run ClickHouse as a native service, so customers get it without leaving the tool they already use. Some are BI and visualization tools that need ClickHouse to show up as a fast, first-class data source behind their dashboards. And some are developer and data platforms we connect through marketplaces and identity federation with a couple of clicks or agentic calls. Every integration is unique, but the goal is the same every time: ClickHouse should feel like a first-class citizen in every environment. The craft is finding the patterns underneath different integrations. As one of the first backend engineers, you'll help shape the technical defaults for this team. You'll have end-to-end ownership, but you'll also work inside the constraints of platforms you don't own: thin documentation, unfamiliar deployment topologies, and timelines governed by partner approval cycles. A lot of the challenge is engineering across trust boundaries you don't fully control. You won't be doing it alone. You'll work closely with your engineering manager, the product manager, a growing team, and experienced engineers across the broader org. If that sounds like your kind of challenge, let's talk. What you'll do You'll own an integration end to end: the design, the code, and the production system that keeps running after launch. The patterns you set there become defaults the rest of the team builds on. Day to day, that looks like: Owning the architecture: auth and identity flows, multi-tenancy, how data moves and where it's allowed to live, performance, and what happens in production Running what you build. Which means owning the infrastructure, CI, deployment, observability behind it and on-call Working on top of external platforms you can't change, and being straight about which risks are yours to manage and which aren't Partnering closely with the internal teams whose services you depend on: iterating on product requirements, agreeing on interfaces and protocols, and proactively finding ways to keep moving About you These are the attributes of someone who will perform well in this role: 8+ years building software, with a good chunk of it on data-heavy or integration-flavored systems Preferably proficient in TypeScript or Go or comfortable contributing to each Solid backend and systems instincts. You can reason about deployment topology, multi-tenancy, and data movement, and you're comfortable owning architectural tradeoffs you'll have to live with later You've worked with modern auth protocols, service principals, and identity federation, and you know how to get it right across a trust boundary You've built on someone else's platform and know what that's actually like: incomplete docs, unintended breaking changes, etc. You're comfortable in ambiguity. You can ship before the spec is finished, make sensible calls under uncertainty, and flag the decisions that'll be hard to undo to your team before we bake them in. You're good with other engineers. Much of the work runs through teams you don't own, and you earn their trust by how you think, not just what you commit. You're mainly a backend engineer, but you're comfortable enough to touch a modern React app You use AI tools well and honestly. Reach for Claude Code, Cursor, Copilot, or whatever helps, and be clear about where you did and didn't You write well. Most of how we coordinate happens async in chats, design docs and RFCs Nice to have None of these are required, but any of them would be a bonus: Close familiarity with a major cloud data or analytics platform ecosystem Real depth in auth and identity federation, or experience building to a partner's security review, marketplace requirements or certification requirements Hands-on experience designing multi-tenant SaaS platforms, or the isolation and deployment topology behind them Working knowledge of ClickHouse, or another columnar / OLAP engine Perks Flexible work environment - ClickHouse is a globally distributed company and remote-friendly. We currently operate in over 25 countries. Healthcare - Employer contributions towards your healthcare. Equity in the company - Every new team member who joins our company receives stock options. Time off - Flexible time off in the US, generous entitlement in other countries. A USD$500 Home office setup if you’re a remote employee. Global Gatherings – We believe in the power of in-person connection and offer opportunities to engage with colleagues at company-wide offsites. Culture - We All Shape It As part of a rapidly scaling start-up, you will be instrumental in shaping our culture. Are you interested in finding out more about our culture? Learn more about our values here . Check out our blog posts or follow us on LinkedIn to find out more about what’s happening at ClickHouse. Equal Opportunity & Privacy ClickHouse provides equal employment opportunities to all employees and applicants and prohibits discrimination and harassment of any type based on factors such as race, color, religion, age, sex, national origin, disability status, genetics, protected veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state or local laws. descriptionAr: About the Team OpenAI’s Compute organization turns ambitious AI research into real-world capability by delivering the compute infrastructure behind our most advanced models. The team works across software, hardware, facilities, operations, and engineering disciplines to make enormous amounts of compute available, reliable, and efficient. As the demand for frontier AI grows, so does the complexity of the systems required to support it. Scaling this infrastructure means solving problems that cut across distributed systems, ML infrastructure, GPU fleets, power, cooling, networking, manufacturing, supply chain, and data center delivery. Our work is focused on expanding the compute foundation that enables OpenAI to train more capable models, including systems like GPT-5.6, and make frontier AI available to more people, products, and workflows. We’re looking for exceptional people across many disciplines to help build the next generation of AI infrastructure at a scale few organizations have attempted. About the Role We are hiring across a broad range of roles to help design, build, scale, and operate OpenAI’s compute infrastructure. Depending on your background, you may work on large-scale distributed systems, ML infrastructure, hardware systems, manufacturing, supply chain, data center development, or the physical engineering systems required to bring massive compute capacity online. You’ll work with teams across research, engineering, hardware, operations, and infrastructure to solve high-impact problems at extraordinary scale. This may include improving system reliability, accelerating deployment timelines, increasing operational efficiency, designing new infrastructure, or helping bring new compute platforms and facilities from concept to production. This is an opportunity to work on one of the most important infrastructure challenges in AI: building the compute foundation required to train and serve increasingly capable frontier models. Key Responsibilities Help build, scale, and operate OpenAI’s global compute infrastructure. Solve complex problems across software, hardware, manufacturing supply chain, and data center systems. Improve the reliability, performance, efficiency, and scalability of critical infrastructure. Partner with cross-functional teams to bring new compute capacity online quickly and reliably. Identify bottlenecks across technical, operational, and physical systems, and develop practical solutions. Build tools, processes, systems, or infrastructure that improve execution at scale. Contribute to the long-term architecture and operational maturity of OpenAI’s compute footprint. Qualifications Have experience building, scaling, or operating complex technical systems. Enjoy working on ambiguous, high-impact problems where the path forward is not always defined. Are comfortable collaborating across disciplines, including software, hardware, operations, and physical infrastructure. Have strong technical judgment and a bias toward execution. Care deeply about reliability, speed, safety, and operational excellence. Are excited by the challenge of building infrastructure at unprecedented scale. Want your work to directly support the development and deployment of frontier AI. Preferred Skills Have experience with AI infrastructure, high-performance computing, distributed systems, GPU clusters, or cloud-scale platforms. Have worked on hardware systems, manufacturing, supply chain, data center development, or large capital infrastructure projects. Have domain expertise in civil, controls, mechanical, hardware, electrical, thermal, power, networking, or facilities engineering. Have helped bring new technical platforms, data centers, factories, or large-scale systems from concept to production. Have experience operating in fast-moving environments where technical depth and execution speed both matter. Co-create the future with us as we build technology that transforms how the world develops software. * Fortune 500® is a registered trademark of Fortune Media IP Limited, used under license. Claim based on GitLab data. Fortune 100 refers to the top 20% ranked companies in the 2025 Fortune 500 list, published in June 2025. An overview of this role Growth Marketing is the activation and delivery arm of GitLab marketing: campaigns, regional and field marketing, lifecycle and product led growth, marketing engineering and operations, corporate events including Transcend, partner marketing, community programs and Co-Create. If a program connects GitLab to a customer or a buyer, it lives here, and the team is accountable for pipeline, first orders, Flex conversion and expansion, and post sale adoption. As Principal Growth Marketing Strategist you work directly with the VP of Growth Marketing as a strategic partner and operator. You hold the whole picture of the engine: the goals every function has committed to, the budget and where it is moving, the strategic projects that do not fit cleanly inside any one function, and the decisions that are waiting on an answer. You keep that picture current, you act on it when the VP is engaged elsewhere, and you use it to move work faster. This is an individual contributor role at the Principal level. You do not manage a team. You manage outcomes across ten functions through influence, judgment and follow through, and you are trusted to speak for Growth Marketing in rooms the VP cannot be in. The people on the leadership team are senior, experienced marketers; they will work with you because you make them faster and sharper, not because of the title. You will be effective in this role if you have led marketing yourself at a senior level, understand how a modern B2B software company makes money, are curious and hands on with AI in your own work, and can move between a budget trade off, a partner negotiation, a pipeline review and a keynote plan in the same day without losing the thread. What you'll do Run Growth Marketing's operating rhythm: goals, business reviews, planning cycles and the metrics inspection behind them, so decisions get made, recorded and followed through. Track commitments across the leadership team between their 1:1s with the VP, so those conversations are about strategy rather than status. Own the strategic projects that matter to Growth Marketing and have no single functional home: scope them, find the owner or be the owner, and land them. Hold the budget picture across the team, prepare trade offs with a recommendation, and act within the authority the VP has delegated in writing. Represent Growth Marketing on the VP's behalf in pipeline reviews, cross functional planning and partner conversations; carry the position in and the decision out. Unblock functional leaders when the VP is engaged elsewhere, or stage the issue so it takes one conversation rather than three. descriptionAr: Perplexity is AI for people who expect more. More accuracy. More agency. More signal, less noise. Our answer engine handles hundreds of millions of queries every month for people whose questions spark change and whose decisions bend the world toward progress. Our legal team works side by side with product and business teams. We help the company move quickly, make sound risk decisions, and build legal requirements into products and operations from the start. About the Opportunity We are looking for a practical, versatile attorney to join our Product, Privacy and Regulatory Legal team. You will have a clear center of gravity in consumer protection and a flexible mandate across product counseling, privacy, regulatory matters, marketing, subscriptions, and international expansion. This is not a narrow subject matter role. You might advise on a new consumer product flow one day, assess an advertising or subscription practice the next, and help respond to a regulator or customer escalation after that. You will work directly with Product, Engineering, Growth, Marketing, Support, Security, GRC, Policy, and Communications. The right person can identify the legal issue quickly, learn the product deeply, and give the business a practical path forward. You will own matters independently and help turn recurring questions into clear guidance and durable systems. This role Reports to the Senior Director, Product, Privacy and Regulatory Legal. What You Will Do Serve as a primary legal partner for consumer products and features from early design through launch and post-launch review Advise on consumer protection issues, including unfair and deceptive practices, disclosures, pricing, subscriptions, renewals, refunds, promotions, advertising claims, dark patterns, and customer support practices Review marketing, growth, and advertising initiatives, including adtech and martech integrations, audience practices, email and messaging campaigns, and product claims Counsel product and engineering teams on privacy, data use, consent, retention, security, AI transparency, age-related protections, and other legal requirements Lead legal review of cross-functional launches and translate complex requirements into practical product and operational choices Support responses to consumer complaints, state attorneys general, competition authorities, privacy authorities, and other regulators around the world, in partnership with the regulatory lead and outside counsel Assess incidents and escalations that cross product, privacy, consumer protection, contractual, and regulatory lines Monitor legal developments affecting AI products and online services, then convert them into clear advice, playbooks, and product requirements Help build scalable legal infrastructure, including templates, review standards, decision records, training, and self-service guidance Flex across the broader Product, Privacy and Regulatory Legal portfolio as company priorities and risk change What We Are Looking For J.D. from an accredited law school, or an LL.M. or equivalent law degree, and current authorization to practice law in the U.S. state where you are located At least five years of relevant legal experience at a law firm, government agency, or in house, with meaningful consumer protection or product counseling experience Strong command of U.S. consumer protection law and enforcement principles, including Section 5 of the FTC Act and state unfair or deceptive acts and practices (UDAP) laws Experience with several of the following areas: subscriptions and auto-renewal, advertising and marketing, privacy and data protection, payments, promotions, platform regulation, or AI governance Ability to lead a product or regulatory matter independently, from fact development through recommendation and execution Excellent judgment. You know what to decide, what to escalate, and how to explain risk without slowing the business unnecessarily Clear, direct writing and the ability to translate legal requirements for product, engineering, and business teams Comfort learning technical systems and asking precise questions about how products, data flows, and controls actually work Hands-on attitude, low ego, intellectual curiosity, and comfort with ambiguity in a fast-moving environment Genuine interest in AI products and the legal questions created by how people use them Bonus Experience at the FTC, a state attorney general's office, or another consumer protection or privacy regulator In-house experience at a consumer technology company, online platform, marketplace, or subscription business Experience handling regulator inquiries, investigations, or consumer class action risk Working knowledge of the CCPA/CPRA, GDPR, state privacy laws, ROSCA, CAN-SPAM, TCPA, COPPA, state auto-renewal laws, or similar international consumer regimes

This strategic position focuses on driving pipeline that meaningfully contribute to Notion's bottom line. This role can be based in either San Francisco or New York City. descriptionAr: About the team OpenAI’s mission is to ensure that artificial general intelligence (AGI) benefits all of humanity. Our Go-To-Market (GTM) organization helps customers adopt and scale OpenAI’s products and platform. The GTM Strategy & Planning team sits within Revenue Operations and works at the intersection of GTM Leadership, Strategic Finance, and the broader business. We shape how OpenAI invests, organizes, and scales its revenue organization, translating company ambitions into actionable growth strategies, financial targets, capacity plans, and investment decisions. Our work spans OpenAI’s global GTM organization, including Sales, Technical Success, Partnerships, and emerging businesses. We partner closely with senior leadership to ensure our resources support the highest-impact opportunities as the business grows. About the role We’re looking for a highly analytical and strategic operator to help shape OpenAI’s GTM growth strategy and operating plan. In this role, you’ll tackle some of the most important questions facing our revenue organization: Where should we invest to accelerate growth? How should we allocate resources across markets, segments, and customer motions? What level of productivity can we expect as we scale? How do we translate ambitious financial goals into executable plans? You’ll own planning and analytical workstreams spanning revenue targets, investment strategy, capacity and productivity modeling, and GTM organizational design. Working closely with Strategic Finance, GTM Leadership, and cross-functional partners, you’ll develop rigorous, data-backed recommendations that inform executive decisions. This role is ideal for someone who combines strong financial and analytical skills with strategic judgment, thrives in ambiguity, and can move between detailed modeling and executive-level decision-making. This role is based in San Francisco, CA or New York, NY. In this role, you will: Partner with GTM Leadership and Strategic Finance to translate company financial objectives into growth strategies, resource allocation decisions, and operating plans across regions, segments, and functions. Build headcount, capacity, and productivity models to inform where and how OpenAI invests across Sales, Technical Success, Partnerships, and other GTM functions. Develop regional, segment, and team-level revenue targets, translating company financial goals into executable plans with clear accountability. Build scenario analyses to evaluate how hiring, productivity, product launches, partner distribution, and other growth levers affect revenue performance and investment requirements. Develop data-driven recommendations on segmentation, coverage models, organizational structure, and resource allocation to support growth and operational efficiency. Lead annual and midyear planning cycles, aligning Strategic Finance, GTM Leadership, Field Operations, Data Science, and other stakeholders around a cohesive operating plan. Analyze revenue attainment, capacity, productivity, and other key performance indicators to surface risks, challenge assumptions, and inform strategic decisions. Translate complex analyses into clear, actionable recommendations for senior leadership, balancing analytical rigor with business judgment and a company-wide perspective. You might thrive in this role if you: Have 8+ years of experience in GTM Strategy & Operations, Strategic Finance, Business Operations, management consulting, or a similarly analytical and strategic role. Have exceptional analytical and financial modeling skills, with experience building complex models that inform strategic, financial, and operational decisions. Understand GTM strategy, revenue planning, capacity models, and the drivers of growth and productivity in high-growth technology businesses. Have experience with SaaS, consumption-based, or usage-based business models and understand how different GTM motions influence revenue growth. Have led complex, cross-functional initiatives, navigated ambiguity, and aligned senior stakeholders with competing priorities. Bring strong strategic judgment and problem-solving skills, including the ability to challenge assumptions, evaluate trade-offs, and develop practical recommendations. Communicate clearly in writing and in conversation, translating complex analyses into executive narratives that influence leadership decisions. Demonstrate ownership, intellectual curiosity, and comfort operating in a fast-paced, evolving environment. You may also bring: Experience in AI, developer platforms, cloud infrastructure, or other technical product businesses. Experience partnering directly with CRO, CFO, or executive leadership teams on strategic planning and investment decisions. Experience designing GTM coverage models, segmentation strategies, or sales productivity frameworks. Experience managing or mentoring team members. About OpenAI OpenAI is an AI research and deployment company dedicated to ensuring that general-purpose artificial intelligence benefits all of humanity. We push the boundaries of the capabilities of AI systems and seek to safely deploy them to the world through our products. AI is an extremely powerful tool that must be created with safety and human needs at its core, and to achieve our mission, we must encompass and value the many different perspectives, voices, and experiences that form the full spectrum of humanity. An overview of this role As a Professional Services Program Manager at GitLab, you will lead the delivery of complex, multi-workstream services engagements for some of our largest and most strategic customers. You will help customers turn transformation goals into clear execution plans by bringing structure, visibility, and accountability across interconnected projects. Working closely with customer stakeholders and GitLab team members, you will guide programs from planning through delivery while building trusted relationships across executive, technical, and delivery teams. In this role, you will define and apply a strong delivery methodology grounded in agile and project management best practices, communicate that approach clearly, and keep teams aligned on milestones, dependencies, and outcomes. This is a strong opportunity to shape how customers adopt GitLab at scale and help them realize meaningful business value through effective program leadership. What you'll do Lead delivery of multi-workstream professional services engagements for large and strategic customers Build strong relationships with customer stakeholders, including executive leaders, program and project managers, engineering, development, and security teams Develop and apply a delivery methodology that uses agile and project management best practices, and communicate how the methodology will be used throughout the program Create and continuously communicate program roadmaps, dependencies, milestones, and deliverables across connected projects Manage stakeholder expectations and secure approval on major milestones, decisions, and delivery plans Define program strategy, including business justification, expected benefits, in-scope and out-of-scope work, timelines, schedules, resources, stakeholders, and success criteria Establish core program structures such as RACI charts, work breakdown structures, communication plans, and escalation paths Work closely with Engagement Managers and Regional Delivery Managers to support program scoping, review delivery assumptions, and help improve project management processes through quarterly objectives and key results (OKRs) What you'll bring Experience leading complex programs with multiple interdependent projects, stakeholders, and timelines Strong skill in program planning, forecasting, reporting, and communicating delivery metrics clearly to internal and external stakeholders Ability to organize, monitor, and manage long-term project budgets, schedules, risks, and dependencies Proven ability to build collaborative relationships with customers and partner effectively with Engagement Managers, Architects, and delivery teams Working knowledge of agile and other project management approaches, with the judgment to apply the right structure to different customer needs Ability to develop long-term plans that support customer adoption, transformation, and successful delivery outcomes Comfort leading program-level meetings and driving progress across multiple workstreams Willingness to complete GitLab Project Management certification within 2 months of starting in the role About the team On our Professional Services team, we help customers adopt GitLab effectively by turning strategy into structured delivery. As Program Managers on our team, we bring clarity to large, complex engagements by coordinating people, plans, and processes across multiple workstreams. We work closely with customers, Engagement Managers, Architects, and delivery leaders to create practical plans, manage risk, and keep programs moving toward agreed outcomes. Because we operate in an all-remote, asynchronous environment, we value clear communication, strong documentation, and ownership. This role is well suited for you if you enjoy building order in complex environments, guiding stakeholders through change, and helping customers make progress on meaningful transformation efforts. Interface with GitLab's product and engineering teams to unblock customer outcomes and share feedback that helps improve GitLab features and services. Mentor Associate and Intermediate Professional Services Engineers, providing technical guidance, helping remove blockers, and supporting increased autonomy. Manage and deliver multiple customer engagements at once, either as the primary engineer or as a lead providing oversight and direction to other engineers. What you’ll bring Professional exposure with one or more infrastructure as code or configuration as code technologies such as Terraform, Ansible, Packer, Puppet, or Chef. Professional exposure with two or more cloud providers such as Amazon Web Services (AWS), Google Cloud Platform (GCP), or Microsoft Azure. Experience delivering customer-facing services such as installation, migration, training, and advisory engagements across GitLab's feature set. Proven ability to independently manage one or more projects and to lead and provide direction to other Professional Services Engineers on complex engagements. Strong communication skills in English, written and verbal, with the ability to provide clear status updates and build consensus with peers and customers in a remote, largely asynchronous environment. Demonstrated ability to take a solution-oriented approach by identifying root causes, proposing options and tradeoffs, and driving issues to resolution while balancing multiple customer engagements in a fast-paced environment. Demonstrated ability to work effectively in a fully remote organization by communicating clearly in writing, documenting decisions, collaborating asynchronously across time zones, and working in ways consistent with GitLab's values. About the team Senior Professional Services Engineers are part of GitLab's Professional Services team. We partner closely with Engagement Managers and Project Managers to deliver consistent outcomes, and we work with GitLab's product and engineering teams to share customer feedback and improve GitLab. Professional Services operates in a fully remote and largely asynchronous environment, collaborating across regions and time zones. The team's challenge is to support customers with a wide range of architectures and deployment models while maintaining high-quality delivery and setting customers up for long-term success. Join Tier 2 on-call rotations to troubleshoot production issues, contribute to root cause analysis, and improve observability and resiliency. Keep an eye on the competitive landscape to help keep GitLab's agent platform best-in-class as more work becomes agentic. Take part in on-call or operational support where your team’s ownership model requires it. Work through complex requirements and legacy constraints to deliver clear solutions while protecting the reliability of this critical system. Use artificial intelligence agents for well-scoped work when they can speed up delivery without sacrificing quality, and critically review their output. Write maintainable code that follows GitLab's standards and contribute to constructive code reviews. Help strengthen reliability by monitoring production health metrics, participating in Tier 2 on-call, troubleshooting incidents, contributing to root cause analysis, and improving observability and resiliency. Share knowledge through code review, technical documentation, and everyday collaboration while learning from others. Lead discovery and scoping from pre-sales through post-sales, translating ambiguous workflow needs into hypothesis-driven problem framing, system requirements, and an execution plan with measurable endpoints. Define and enforce launch criteria for regulated contexts, including validation evidence, audit readiness, outcome metrics, and drive delivery until we demonstrate sustained production impact. Build in sensitive scientific data environments where auditability, validation, and access controls shape architecture, operating procedures, and failure handling. Run evaluation loops that measure model and system quality against workflow-specific scientific benchmarks and use results to drive model and product changes. Distill deployment learnings into hardened primitives, reference architectures, validation templates, and benchmark harnesses that scale across regulated life sciences environments. You might thrive in this role if you: Bring 5+ years of software/ML engineering or technical deployment experience with customer-facing ownership in biotech, pharma, clinical research, or scientific software; PhD, MS, or equivalent applied experience in a life sciences relevant field encouraged. Have owned customer GenAI deployments end-to-end from scoping through production adoption, and improved them through evaluation design, error analysis, and iterative evidence generation that tightens acceptance criteria over time. Have delivered AI systems in trial design, regulatory writing, or scientific operations where validation strategy, auditability, compliance constraints, and reviewer expectations shaped system design and rollout. Communicate clearly across scientific, clinical, model research, technical, and executive audiences, translating technical tradeoffs into decision quality, risk posture, and measurable outcomes with credibility. descriptionAr: Who are we? Cohere is the leading security-first enterprise AI company. We build cutting-edge foundation AI models and end-to-end products that are designed to solve real-world business problems. We’re training and deploying frontier models for enterprises who are building AI systems. We believe that our work is instrumental to the widespread adoption of AI and we are looking for folks that want to be part of that. We obsess over what we build. Each one of us is responsible for contributing to increasing the capabilities of our models and the value they drive for our customers. Cohere is a team of researchers, engineers, designers, and more, who are all passionate about their craft. We are a global technology company headquartered in Toronto with key offices in London, New York City, San Francisco, Montreal, Paris, Berlin and Seoul. Join us! Why this role? Cohere seeks an experienced and passionate VP of Services, Customer Success & Support to lead our Customer Success and Support teams. In this role, you will be responsible for leading and developing a talented post-sales Customer Success and Support team, who are the primary owners of business and technical relationships with our customers. The ideal candidate will have a background leading post-sales teams in the ML/AI/Data Engineering industry. In this role you will: Drive product adoption and customer experience for our largest customers. Define the customer lifecycle including roles and responsibilities, handoffs, and workflow & influence the product roadmap. Lead customer-facing teams, including coaching sub-function leaders (Customer Success, Services, Technical Support) to ensure that all teams are aligned and focused on delivering an exceptional customer experience. Measure and analyze customer data to identify trends and areas for improvement, including analyzing customer feedback, support metrics, and other customer-related data to develop insights that can be used to improve the customer experience, troubleshoot issues and showcase Cohere’s value proposition. Enhance the customer journey, identifying the key touch points across interactions with customers and developing strategies to optimize each step of the journey. Champion the customer within the organization, advocating for the customer in all decision-making processes at the executive level to ensure that customer needs are taken into account when making strategic decisions. Collaborate and partner with other internal teams (pre-sales, Product Management, Machine Learning Engineerings) to ensure that the voice of the customer is represented in strategic decisions. You may be a good fit, if you have: 10+ years of leadership experience developing top-performing teams in Customer Success, Technical Support and Services. Work experience in the AI, ML, Data Engineering, Cloud, SaaS or Tech Infra industry. Proven experiences being highly focussed on customer needs, you're an amazing relationship builder and you can proactively spot opportunities to engage customers and build loyalty. An exceptional collaborative mindset and know how to engage and communicate with leadership and technical & non-technical stakeholders. Strong experience building strategy, a willingness to execute and build from the ground up & are always willing to dig deeper and jump in when it comes to our customers. Full-Time Employees at Cohere enjoy these Perks: A weekly lunch stipend of $75/£75 or equivalent in your local currency for lunch. Full health and dental benefits, including a separate budget for mental health. RRSP matching, 401K, Pension Scheme. 100% Parental Leave top-up for up to 6 months, for either parent. Annual enrichment benefits: Arts & culture, fitness/wellness, quality time, and a workspace improvement credit. Education & learning stipend for conferences, courses, and coaching. 6 weeks of paid vacation (30 working days!) Budget for traveling to other offices if you are remote, plus an annual company offsite. For those in the office: a daily lunch program, plenty of snacks, and regular community and social events. For those not near an office: a co-working benefit so you can work alongside others in your city. Everyone receives a $500 home office stipend to set up your workspace properly. We strive to create an inclusive work environment for all; we welcome applicants from all backgrounds and are committed to providing equal opportunities. Should you require any accommodations during the recruitment process, please submit an Accommodations Request Form , and we will work together to meet your needs. We may use AI-enabled tools to screen and assess applicants against the criteria for this position. This helps our recruiters identify potentially qualified candidates, but it doesn't limit the applications our recruiters may review or consider. Beware of Scams: Cohere will never ask for payment or third-party services (e.g., CV writing) as part of our hiring process. All legitimate roles are listed on the Cohere careers page and LinkedIn only, with all communications from Cohere employees coming from an @cohere.com or @cw.cohere email alias. If jobs are viewed on other sites then please verify these through our official careers page.

summaryAr: Hi 👋🏾, I’m Abhik , Ashby’s Co-Founder and CTO. Ashby is growing fast, which means exponential growth across every product metric: jobs, applications, interviews, you name it. We’re not slowing down, and as a result, keeping Ashby performant and reliable is a company priority. We need your leadership to do that now and in the future. We’ve already assembled a fantastic Platform & Infrastructure team of 11 engineers
descriptionAr: Hi 👋🏾, I’m Abhik , Ashby’s Co-Founder and CTO. Ashby is growing fast, which means exponential growth across every product metric: jobs, applications, interviews, you name it. We’re not slowing down, and as a result, keeping Ashby performant and reliable is a company priority. We need your leadership to do that now and in the future. We’ve already assembled a fantastic Platform & Infrastructure team of 11 engineers (all Senior+, >70% Staff), and they’ve done an excellent job handling our growth, but the management and leadership of Platform & Infrastructure have been diffused across our Engineering leaders. As we hit our next level of scale, it’s time for us to hire an Engineering leader responsible for performance and reliability, and for building out the team that ensures those. Hopefully, that’s you! The Role In this role, you will report directly to me, and your responsibilities will include: Building and maintaining a long-term vision and 6-month roadmap for Platform & Infrastructure. Growing the Platform & Infrastructure team. You’ll hire ICs, managers, and build out a headcount plan. This will include determining if more specialized roles need to be established (e.g., DB Admin). Building and maintaining an excellent relationship with Product Engineering. The ideal state is that Product Engineering can move incredibly fast independently without breaking performance or reliability, and Platform & Infrastructure doesn’t feel like they’re always cleaning up someone else’s “mess.” Today, there’s a great relationship, but there’s always room for improvement! Assessing and improving our monitoring and incident management process. Again, we’re doing relatively well here, but there’s always room to improve. For example, making uptime measurement easier and improving coordination with Support during incidents. Maintaining vendor relationships and negotiating pricing for our critical hosting and observability infrastructure , including AWS, ClickHouse, Datadog, and Braintrust. They have a meaningful impact on gross margin and need to be kept in check. You’ve managed managers. Managing other leaders is a very different ball game, and not everyone enjoys it or thrives in it. Within your first 6 months, you’ll most likely have to hire a manager underneath you. If you have experience managing developer experience and developer tools, building out a dedicated team for DevEx . If you don’t have experience here, DevEx will report into Product Engineering. Happy to discuss once we meet! A big part of our secret sauce is how we run Engineering. We achieve incredible speed and quality by discarding many industry norms and being optimistic about Engineers. We consider what makes exceptional Engineers exceptional, then figure out how to hire them and build an environment that gives them the freedom and agency to be exceptional. You’ll be a key leader in ensuring that continues! The Qualifications We’re entrusting you with a company priority, so we want you to know how to scale products and build the great teams that do that. This means: You played an important role leading a company through a high-growth period (either as an IC Lead or Engineering Leader). You had to make high-quality decisions under pressure. That often meant striking a balance between short-term fixes to keep the product from falling over and long-term investments to ensure it didn’t happen again. You have experience hiring and building hiring processes, and enjoy it! You’ve designed interviews, interview loops, and led hiring strategy. You have a track record of excellent collaboration with other departments. You were a key contributor to company-level initiatives that involved Product Engineering, Product, Sales, or Support. Those departments felt heard and supported, yet positively challenged by you. You have a background in writing production software (far beyond scripts). Our Platform & Infrastructure team is exclusively made up of strong software engineers, not just folks who scale the systems software runs on. They can jump into any part of our app, understand the code, and modify the underlying logic. We expect you to have similar experience to grow and upskill the team. You are knowledgeable about platform and infrastructure technologies, networking, and hardware. You know how Kubernetes goes beyond a Container Orchestration Platform, how traffic flows between Load Balancers and Pods, and how the intricacies of the underlying hardware can cause Cloud abstractions to break, etc. You are a great communicator, particularly in writing. You’ll need to be able to go deep with Infrastructure Engineers in conversations while also communicating those concepts to folks like myself who have much less experience. You should be comfortable managing a team spanning from the Americas West Coast to Europe. You’ll be able to hire managers to focus on specific time zones, but I expect you to have skips with some engineers (and you should want to, too!). To ensure a reasonable work schedule, we’re only hiring candidates who live in the PST-GMT time zone. What We’re Building As engineers, we are used to tooling that makes us better at what we do. When we started Ashby, we saw the opposite with Talent Acquisition software. Recruiting teams were leveling up how they did their work, but instead of software meeting this new standard, it held them back. Scheduling a final round is an excellent example. Recruiting teams wanted to schedule candidates faster, track interviewer preparation and quality, and do it with half the headcount. A recruiter needed to manually collect availability from the candidate, identify qualified interviewers, perform “Calendar Tetris” to find who is available to interview the candidate, schedule on the earliest date possible, and make any last-minute adjustments as availability changed. They must do this while considering the interview load on each individual and whether interviewers need to be trained and shadowing others

descriptionAr: About Sentry Software runs the world and the pace is faster than ever. Trusted by 200,000+ organizations, Sentry is today’s application monitoring standard and our team is building its AI-native future. About the role You’ll join the team behind Sentry’s Size Analysis and Snapshots, two products that check every pull request before it ships. Size Analysis breaks down iOS and Android builds to explain why an app got bigger. Snapshots catches unintended visual changes by diffing screenshots against a baseline. Both run in our customers’ CI, report straight to Source Code Management providers, and handle some of the heaviest payloads at Sentry: multi-GB app binaries and builds with tens of thousands of images. In this role you will You’ll work full-stack with a backend lean, owning features from the moment a build arrives from CI, to the moment when UI engineers use that data to decide whether to merge. You’ll own the codebase behind our mobile binary analysis and large-scale image comparison. You’ll share the pipeline, the GitHub integration and on-call with the rest of the Sentry team. Build and tune the backend services and task-based pipelines that ingest, analyze and compare builds, with large artifacts in object storage, fast and reliable on multi-GB binaries and changesets with tens of thousands of screenshots Extend our product: own the functionality end-to-end, react on feedback and come up with proposals for further product development. Own the GitHub integration end to end: PR status checks, comments, approvals and webhooks, including races, duplicates and missing-baseline edge cases Ship frontend features such as treemaps, build comparisons and diff viewers that stay fast on huge datasets Run what you build: deploys across regions, metrics, logging and on-call, and be the person who debugs the weird customer build You’ll love this job if you Want your work to show up in the pull requests our customers open every day, not buried in a dashboard nobody checks Like problems with real weight: a multi-GB IPA, tens of thousands of screenshots in a single build, a binary format with sparse documentation Would rather own a feature from upload to UI than hand off half of it (end-to-end ownership) Enjoy building for developers, who will tell you exactly what’s wrong and why Want to help two products that started at a startup grow into core parts of Sentry Qualifications 3+ years building production web services, with strong Python (Django preferred) and a habit of typed, tested code Working proficiency in React and TypeScript, enough to ship a full feature without handing off the frontend Experience with async task systems and event pipelines (Kafka, task queues, worker pools), including idempotency, locking, retries and their failure modes Experience with Postgres schema design and migrations that work under rolling deploys, plus pragmatic rollout habits like feature flags and revertable changes A track record of performance work: profiling, parallelism, memory reduction and large-file streaming through object storage Bonus points for: Hands-on experience with mobile build artifacts and tooling (LIEF, bundletool, apksigner, link maps, DWARF, code signing) Image processing or pixel-diff tooling GitHub Apps or the Checks API Data visualization, especially treemaps Prior work on developer tools, CI or observability products We are obliged by law to quote the minimum wage of EUR 60,844,-- gross per year for this position, in accordance with the respective collective agreement (IT-KV). The salary that Sentry offers you is adjusted to the current market situation and will be above the IT-KV. A successful candidate will be eligible to participate in Sentry’s employee benefit plans/programs applicable to the candidate’s position (including incentive compensation, equity grants, paid time off, and group health insurance coverage). Founded in 2019, Linear has become the platform of choice for more than 50,000 companies (including OpenAI, Coinbase, and Ramp) to plan, build, and ship their products. Over the past few years, Linear has experienced incredible organic growth and has become the default tool of choice for many of the world’s best product teams. We are now layering a product-led sales motion on top of our existing self-serve business to further accelerate our ambitions and bring the magic of Linear to even more and larger companies. As an Account Executive at Linear, you’ll contribute to the future of our product and help high-impact companies build better software. Location & work mode While Linear is a remote-first company across the US and Europe, this role is specifically based in London. We’re looking for someone who can work from our London office in Shoreditch 3 days per week (Mondays, Tuesdays, Thursdays), as this role will be closely connected to in-person collaboration with our growing sales presence in the region. What you'll do Become a product expert and help customers use Linear effectively; assist prospects through the trial and evaluation phase Generate a strong pipeline and exceed quarterly and annual targets Build relationships with key stakeholders within accounts Stay up to date with our product offering, industry trends, competitive landscape, and market trends to continuously adapt sales strategies and approaches for maximum impact Be the voice of the customer; advocate for customers by surfacing product or adoption blockers to our product team What we're looking for 5+ years in a quota-carrying sales role Experience selling to a technical audience; bonus if you have previous experience working with a collaboration or developer tool SaaS and startup experience; comfortable working and adapting in a fast-paced and flexible environment Strong written and verbal communication, presentation, and product demonstration skills Highly autonomous with a bias for action. Owner’s mindset to quickly come up to speed on product, market, ICP, and unique differentiators What we offer We're a small, focused team that cares deeply about the quality of our work and the people we do it with.
